problem: The example counts a 500 MB application layer for each of the 10 copies, but the same section says image layers are read-only and shared and that ten containers from one image share layers instead of copying them. Ten copies of the same application would share the 500 MB app layer too, giving 0.1 + 0.5 = 0.6 GB, not 5.1 GB. As written, a student learns that only the base is shared and that app layers are always copied per container, which is wrong.
fix: State the assumption explicitly: 'Assume each copy has its own distinct application layer (for example, a different build), so only the 100 MB base is shared.' Add the contrast: 'If all ten ran the identical image, the 500 MB app layer would also be shared and the total would be 0.6 GB.' Do the same in Q6.

problem: Section 1 defines the hypervisor as the layer that owns the physical CPU, memory and devices (a Type 1 hypervisor). The figure puts the hypervisor above a host OS, which is a Type 2 layout where the hypervisor reaches hardware through the host OS and does not own the devices directly.
fix: Add one line: 'A Type 1 hypervisor sits directly on hardware; a Type 2 hypervisor runs as a program on a host OS, as in the figure.' Or put the hypervisor beside the host OS in the diagram.

problem: The first column heading is 'Question', but the rows are attributes (Guest OS, Start, Image, Isolation, Best for), not questions. The Guest OS row also does not answer its own question for containers: 'shared host kernel' is the reason, not the value.
fix: Rename the column 'Aspect'. Change the container cell of the Guest OS row to 'none — shares the host kernel'.

problem: The formula VM image = guest OS + app + data puts stored application data inside the image. In practice application data sits on separate volumes or disks and is not part of the image, and the worked example never counts any data.
fix: Say 'VM image = guest OS + app (plus any data baked into the image)', and note that live application data usually lives on separate volumes and is not counted here.

problem: 'Only the changed blocks' is imprecise. With overlay filesystems, the common Docker storage driver, a modified file is copied whole on first write (file granularity); only block-level drivers copy individual blocks.
fix: Write 'copy-on-write stores only the changed data — whole files with overlay-style drivers, single blocks with block-level drivers — instead of the full image.' Use the same wording in Q7.
